_comment: GitHub repository role -> SonarQube Cloud project permission mapping.
JSON has no comment syntax, so keys starting with an underscore hold the
documentation. gh_to_sqc_permissions.py ignores them all except for
'_sqc_permissions', which it reads: those keys are the only permissions
accepted under 'roles', and their values are the corresponding names in the
SonarQube Cloud UI. This file is therefore the single source of truth for
the permission list - the script hard-codes nothing.
The values under 'roles' are the raw permission keys that the script sends
as the 'permission' parameter of /api/permissions/add_user_to_template and
/api/permissions/add_group_to_template. They mean:
user                 -> Browse Project
See the project and its measures, issues and pages.
codeviewer           -> See Source Code
View the source code of the project.
issueadmin           -> Administer Issues
Resolve, reopen, assign and change the severity of issues.
securityhotspotadmin -> Administer Security Hotspots
Change the status of a Security Hotspot.
architectureadmin    -> Administer Architecture
Edit the project's intended architecture. Without it
the architecture editor is read-only; viewing the
architecture map needs no permission. Not granted by
any role below by default - add it where you want it.
scan                 -> Execute Analysis
Run an analysis and push results to the project.
admin                -> Administer Project
Change the project configuration, permissions and settings.
The five keys under 'roles' are the GitHub repository roles. All five must
be present. An empty list is allowed and means the role grants nothing on
SonarQube Cloud, in which case those users and teams are reported as
skipped. Order inside a list does not matter and duplicates are ignored.
GitHub's legacy API permission names are normalised before lookup:
pull -> read, push -> write, triage/maintain/admin are unchanged.
_sqc_permissions_comment: Read by the script: the permitted values under 'roles', mapped to their
names in the SonarQube Cloud UI. Only remove an entry here if SonarQube
Cloud stops accepting it; removing one that is still used under 'roles'
makes the script exit with a configuration error.
These are the seven project permissions SonarQube Cloud accepts, as listed
parameter. An entry here is merely available for use - it grants nothing
until a role under 'roles' references it. 'architectureadmin' is present
_admin_users_comment: OPTIONAL. Extra users who should administer the project regardless of what
GitHub says. Use it for the people who own the SonarQube Cloud side and are
'logins' holds SonarQube Cloud logins (for GitHub-authenticated users this
is usually the GitHub login, sometimes suffixed with the provider, e.g.
'jsmith@github'). Leave the list empty - or delete the whole 'admin_users'
object - to disable the feature entirely.
Every login is checked against the organization's members exactly like a
GitHub collaborator: one that does not exist on SonarQube Cloud is reported
as skipped rather than failing the run.
'permissions' is what each of these users receives. The default grants
Administer Project and See Source Code, plus Browse Project - without
'user' a person cannot open the project in the UI at all, which would make
the other two useless. Values must be keys of '_sqc_permissions' above.
A login that is ALSO a GitHub collaborator keeps both sets of permissions:
the role mapping and this list are combined, never one instead of the other.
